NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a coupled oil-level minimization and breather-condition-gated load-ramp procedure that reduces air entrainment at the source and suppresses transient foam nucleation during cold starts. Standard practice sets a single static oil level (often at or above mid-sight-glass) and applies full load immediately after startup, ignoring breather restriction as a foam driver. The departure is the COUPLING of the oil-level setpoint to the breather maintenance state via a mandatory cold-start load ramp: the oil level is set to the manufacturer's minimum safe level (reducing churning volume), and a time/temperature-gated load ramp is enforced after every startup until the breather is verified clean — the arrangement element that is the departure is the CONDITIONAL LOAD RAMP SCHEDULE keyed to breather condition.

ADJACENT-TECHNIQUE CLEARANCE
Closest existing practice: wind-turbine gearbox "run-in" procedures that ramp load over hours for new installations. Difference: this intervention applies a SHORT (15 min), REPEATABLE (every startup), CONDITIONAL (breather-state-gated) ramp to an IN-SERVICE splash-lubricated gearbox using ONLY existing controls — no new hardware, no extended downtime, no oil change.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: air entrainment rate ∝ (gear tip speed)³ × (submerged gear volume) × (1 − foam stability). Foam stability ∝ defoamer concentration × (1 + pressure fluctuation amplitude). 
- Reducing oil level to minimum safe level cuts submerged gear volume by ~30–40% (typical helical gearbox: mid-level to min-level drops immersed face width by 1/3), directly reducing air entrainment rate by same factor. 
- Breather restriction causes ±5–10 kPa pressure swings during cold start (viscous oil + restricted vent); the load ramp holds gear speed low while oil warms, cutting tip-speed-cubed term by (0.3)³ ≈ 0.03 for the ramp duration, allowing foam to collapse before full-speed churning begins. 
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = air entrainment rate (volume air entrained per minute); the mechanism moves it DOWN by reducing submerged gear volume (oil level) and by staging tip speed via load ramp; this REDUCES foam generation and mesh film collapse.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: On a gearbox exhibiting the failure (foam visible at sight glass, micropitting on inspection), apply the three intervention elements simultaneously. Run identical duty cycle (load profile, hours) for 2000 hours. 
Instruments: Existing sight glass (foam height), existing oil temperature sensor (ramp gate), oil sample port (ASTM D3427 air release, foam tendency ASTM D892), magnetic plug / filter debris (micropitting proxy), vibration transducer on bearing housing (bearing distress). 
Pass/Fail thresholds: 
- Foam height at sight glass < 10% of sump headspace at steady full load (visual, weekly) 
- Air release time (ASTM D3427, 50°C) ≤ 10 min (baseline typically 20–60 min in foaming condition) 
- Foam tendency (ASTM D892, Seq I) ≤ 100 ml foam after 10 min settling 
- Ferrous debris rate (mg/1000 hr) ≤ 50% of pre-intervention baseline 
- No new micropitting on gears/bearings at 2000 hr borescope inspection 
Duration: 2000 operating hours (minimum 3 breather maintenance intervals). 
Kill criterion: If foam height exceeds 25% headspace at any weekly check, or debris rate increases >20% over baseline at 500 hr, intervention fails — revert and investigate breather/oil level compliance.
